notes: String-obbligato R&B — the research's own name for the board: "a written instrumental counterline as the hook, from 90s ballads to 2000s crossover pop-R&B", 1994–2009. The band is "62–95 half-time-and-straight mix, plus one 130 crossover outlier"; the entry states no boundary between its two halves, so the declared 62–95 is kept whole; the half-time reading is the encoded one (`halfTime` true, `halftime_3`, from the entry's "beat 3 at the doubled count on ballads"), and the 130 outlier is modelled under the artist it belongs to rather than here. ⚠ The bpm mode is INFERRED: the entry names no tempo inside 62–95 at all, so 74 is this author's centre of gravity, not a reading. Three drum deltas: "kick on 1 and the 8th before 3" at one or two hits with syncopation 0.1, "layered clap-plus-snare on the backbeat" offset 1–4 ms, and "16th hats only in the hook" at 0.16 fill density — plus the board's habit of "tambourine on the backbeat", a downbeat tambourine lane with `tambourineMirrorsClap` true. The identifying parameter is the countermelody, and the research names it as *the* parameter: "the **obbligato string line** — a written violin counterline running through the whole record (Bruce Dukov on 'Thong Song', modelled on Wes Montgomery's reading of 'Eleanor Rigby')". So `countermelody.densityRatio` is 0.72, the highest in this section, with three styles alive at +12 — a line that plays for the length of the record, not an answer at the end of a phrase. "Under it sit 4-chord m7/maj7 cycles", so the chord families run four deep with a 0.16 triad share. Their signature climax — a semitone lift into the final chorus — has no schema field and is recorded here. The bass is "rounded synth bass on roots with a glide into the downbeat", so a 0.38 `glideProb` and no `bass808` block. ⚠ Every velocity and density number is INFERRED. ⚠ `session.keys` is part-sourced: the entry names `C#m`, `Dm`, and the remaining values `Fm`, `Bbm`, together with all 4 weights, are INFERRED rather than read from the entry.
